conditions.name: Tension Headache / Migraine
conditions.description: A common condition causing pain and pressure in the head, often related to stress, tension, or dehydration.
recommendations: Rest in a quiet, dark room
Stay hydrated and drink water
Take over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen
Apply a cold or warm compress to your forehead
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If headaches are severe, sudden, recurring frequently, or accompanied by vision changes, confusion, or fever.

conditions.name: Fever / Viral Infection
conditions.description: An elevated body temperature, usually a sign that the body is fighting an infection.
recommendations: Rest and get plenty of sleep
Stay hydrated with water, juice, or broth
Take fever-reducing medication such as acetaminophen
Wear light clothing and use a light blanket
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If fever exceeds 103°F (39.4°C), lasts more than 3 days, or is accompanied by severe headache, stiff neck, rash, or difficulty breathing.

conditions.name: Common Cold / Upper Respiratory Infection
conditions.description: A reflex action to clear the airways, commonly caused by viral infections, allergies, or irritants.
recommendations: Drink warm fluids like tea with honey
Use cough drops or lozenges to soothe the throat
Use a humidifier to add moisture to the air
Avoid smoke and other irritants
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If cough lasts more than 3 weeks, produces blood or thick green/yellow mucus, or is accompanied by shortness of breath or wheezing.

conditions.name: Fatigue / Chronic Tiredness
conditions.description: Persistent tiredness that is not relieved by rest, potentially caused by lifestyle factors, stress, or underlying conditions.
recommendations: Improve sleep hygiene — aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep
Exercise regularly, even a short daily walk helps
Eat a balanced diet rich in iron and vitamins
Manage stress through relaxation techniques
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If fatigue is severe, persistent for more than 2 weeks, or accompanied by unexplained weight loss, pain, or mood changes.

conditions.name: Nausea / Digestive Upset
conditions.description: An uneasy sensation in the stomach often preceding vomiting, caused by various factors including food, motion, or illness.
recommendations: Sip clear fluids slowly — water, ginger ale, or electrolyte drinks
Eat bland foods like crackers, rice, or toast
Avoid greasy, spicy, or heavy foods
Rest and avoid sudden movements
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If nausea persists for more than 48 hours, is accompanied by severe abdominal pain, blood in vomit, or signs of dehydration.

conditions.name: Sore Throat / Pharyngitis
conditions.description: Pain, scratchiness, or irritation of the throat that often worsens when swallowing.
recommendations: Gargle with warm salt water several times a day
Drink warm liquids like tea with honey
Use throat lozenges or sprays for temporary relief
Rest your voice and stay hydrated
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If sore throat is severe, lasts more than a week, or is accompanied by high fever, rash, joint pain, or difficulty breathing.

conditions.name: Back Pain / Muscle Strain
conditions.description: Pain in the upper or lower back, commonly caused by muscle strain, poor posture, or prolonged sitting.
recommendations: Apply ice for the first 48 hours, then switch to heat
Maintain gentle movement — avoid prolonged bed rest
Practice good posture and ergonomic sitting
Take over-the-counter anti-inflammatory medication
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If pain radiates down the legs, causes numbness/tingling, follows an injury, or is accompanied by bladder/bowel issues.

conditions.name: Abdominal Pain / Gastritis
conditions.description: Pain or discomfort in the abdominal area, which can be caused by indigestion, gas, infection, or inflammation.
recommendations: Eat smaller, more frequent meals
Avoid spicy, fatty, or acidic foods
Try over-the-counter antacids for mild cases
Apply a warm compress to the abdomen
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If pain is severe, localized to one area, accompanied by fever, vomiting blood, or persists for more than 24 hours.

conditions.name: Dizziness / Vertigo
conditions.description: A sensation of unsteadiness, lightheadedness, or the feeling that the room is spinning.
recommendations: Sit or lie down immediately when feeling dizzy
Stay hydrated and eat regular meals
Avoid sudden changes in position
Limit caffeine, alcohol, and tobacco
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If dizziness is recurrent, accompanied by fainting, hearing loss, severe headache, or numbness in limbs.

conditions.name: Chest Discomfort / Musculoskeletal Pain
conditions.description: Pain or discomfort in the chest area. While often musculoskeletal, chest pain should always be evaluated to rule out cardiac causes.
symptoms: pain worsening with movement or breathing
recommendations: IMPORTANT: If pain is sudden, severe, or accompanied by shortness of breath, call emergency services immediately
For mild musculoskeletal chest pain, rest and take OTC pain relievers
Avoid strenuous activity until evaluated
Monitor for additional symptoms like arm pain, jaw pain, or sweating
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: IMMEDIATELY if accompanied by shortness of breath, arm/jaw pain, sweating, or nausea. These could indicate a cardiac emergency.

conditions.name: Anxiety Symptoms
conditions.description: Feelings of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome. A common mental health condition.
recommendations: Practice deep breathing exercises — inhale 4 seconds, hold 4, exhale 4
Engage in regular physical activity
Limit caffeine and alcohol intake
Consider mindfulness or meditation practices
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If anxiety significantly interferes with daily life, causes panic attacks, or is accompanied by depression or substance use.

conditions.name: Insomnia / Sleep Difficulty
conditions.description: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or getting restful sleep despite adequate opportunity.
recommendations: Maintain a consistent sleep schedule — same bedtime and wake time daily
Avoid screens for at least 30 minutes before bed
Keep your bedroom cool, dark, and quiet
Avoid caffeine after 2 PM and heavy meals before bed
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If insomnia persists for more than 3 weeks, severely affects daily functioning, or is accompanied by breathing difficulties during sleep.

conditions.name: Seasonal Allergies / Allergic Rhinitis
conditions.description: An immune system response to airborne allergens like pollen, dust, or pet dander.
recommendations: Take over-the-counter antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine)
Keep windows closed during high pollen days
Shower after spending time outdoors
Use a HEPA air purifier indoors
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If symptoms are severe, OTC medications are not effective, or if you experience wheezing or difficulty breathing.

conditions.name: Diarrhea / Gastroenteritis
conditions.description: Frequent loose or watery bowel movements, often caused by viral infection, bacteria, or food intolerance.
recommendations: Stay hydrated with oral rehydration solutions or clear fluids
Follow the BRAT diet: bananas, rice, applesauce, toast
Avoid dairy, fatty, and high-fiber foods temporarily
Wash hands frequently to prevent spreading infection
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If diarrhea lasts more than 3 days, contains blood, is accompanied by high fever, or shows signs of severe dehydration.

conditions.name: Joint Pain / Arthralgia
conditions.description: Pain, stiffness, or swelling in one or more joints, commonly caused by overuse, injury, or inflammation.
recommendations: Rest the affected joint and avoid overuse
Apply ice for swelling or heat for stiffness
Take anti-inflammatory medication like ibuprofen
Gentle stretching and low-impact exercise can help
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If joint pain is sudden, severe, accompanied by significant swelling, redness, warmth, or follows an injury.

conditions.name: Skin Rash / Dermatitis
conditions.description: A noticeable change in the texture or color of the skin, which may be itchy, bumpy, or inflamed.
recommendations: Avoid scratching the affected area
Apply a gentle moisturizer or hydrocortisone cream
Identify and avoid potential irritants or allergens
Take an antihistamine for itching
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If rash is widespread, painful, blistering, accompanied by fever, or does not improve within a week.

conditions.name: Shortness of Breath / Dyspnea
conditions.description: A sensation of not getting enough air, which can range from mild discomfort to a medical emergency.
recommendations: IMPORTANT: If sudden and severe, call emergency services immediately
Sit upright to help open airways
Practice pursed-lip breathing — breathe in through nose, out through pursed lips
Remove yourself from any irritants like smoke or fumes
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: IMMEDIATELY if breathing difficulty is sudden, severe, or accompanied by chest pain, bluish lips, or confusion.

conditions.name: Constipation
conditions.description: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements, typically defined as fewer than three per week.
recommendations: Increase dietary fiber — fruits, vegetables, whole grains
Drink plenty of water throughout the day
Exercise regularly to stimulate bowel function
Consider over-the-counter fiber supplements if needed
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If constipation is persistent, accompanied by blood in stool, severe abdominal pain, or unexplained weight loss.

conditions.name: Eye Strain / Digital Eye Fatigue
conditions.description: Discomfort or fatigue of the eyes after prolonged use of screens, reading, or focusing on close work.
recommendations: Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Adjust screen brightness and reduce glare
Use artificial tears for dry eyes
Ensure proper lighting when reading or working
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If eye pain is severe, vision changes are sudden, or symptoms persist despite rest and lifestyle changes.

conditions.name: Muscle Pain / Myalgia
conditions.description: Pain or soreness in muscles, commonly caused by overuse, tension, stress, or minor injuries.
recommendations: Rest the affected muscles and avoid overexertion
Apply ice initially, then heat after 48 hours
Gentle stretching and light massage can provide relief
Take over-the-counter pain medication as needed
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If muscle pain is severe, persists for more than a week, is accompanied by swelling, redness, or begins after starting a new medication.

conditions.name: Ear Pain / Otitis
conditions.description: Pain in one or both ears, commonly caused by infection, fluid buildup, or changes in pressure.
recommendations: Apply a warm compress to the affected ear
Take over-the-counter pain relievers
Avoid inserting objects into the ear canal
Keep the ear dry — avoid swimming until resolved
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If ear pain is severe, lasts more than 2 days, is accompanied by high fever, discharge, or significant hearing loss.

conditions.name: Common Cold / Influenza
conditions.description: Viral infections affecting the upper respiratory tract, with flu symptoms typically being more severe than cold.
recommendations: Rest as much as possible to help your body recover
Stay hydrated with warm fluids
Use OTC decongestants and pain relievers for symptom relief
Cover coughs and sneezes to prevent spreading
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If symptoms are severe, last more than 10 days, include high persistent fever, or if you are in a high-risk group.

conditions.name: Dehydration
conditions.description: Occurs when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, affecting normal body functions.
recommendations: Drink small, frequent sips of water or oral rehydration solutions
Avoid caffeine and alcohol as they can worsen dehydration
Eat water-rich foods like watermelon, cucumbers, and oranges
Rest in a cool environment
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If experiencing severe thirst, very dark urine, rapid heartbeat, confusion, or fainting.

conditions.name: Heartburn / Acid Reflux (GERD)
conditions.description: A burning sensation in the chest caused by stomach acid flowing back into the esophagus.
recommendations: Avoid trigger foods: spicy, fatty, citrus, chocolate, coffee
Eat smaller meals and do not lie down for 2-3 hours after eating
Elevate the head of your bed slightly
Try over-the-counter antacids for occasional relief
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If heartburn occurs more than twice a week, interferes with daily life, or is accompanied by difficulty swallowing or unintended weight loss.

conditions.name: Toothache / Dental Pain
conditions.description: Pain in or around a tooth, commonly caused by tooth decay, infection, gum disease, or injury.
recommendations: Rinse mouth with warm salt water
Take over-the-counter pain medication
Apply a cold compress to the outside of the cheek
Avoid very hot, cold, or sweet foods and drinks
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: See a dentist promptly if pain is severe, lasts more than 2 days, involves swelling, fever, or discharge.

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Symptoms
conditions.description: Symptoms affecting urination, often indicating a urinary tract infection or other urological condition.
recommendations: Drink plenty of water to help flush the urinary tract
Avoid caffeine, alcohol, and spicy foods that can irritate the bladder
Urinate frequently — do not hold it in
Wipe from front to back to prevent bacterial spread
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: Promptly if symptoms are present — UTIs typically require prescription antibiotics. See a doctor if there is blood in urine, fever, or back pain.

conditions.name: Low Mood / Depression Symptoms
conditions.description: Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest, or hopelessness that affect daily functioning.
recommendations: Reach out to a trusted friend, family member, or counselor
Maintain a daily routine with regular sleep and meals
Engage in physical activity — even a short walk can help
Limit alcohol and avoid recreational drugs
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If feelings persist for more than 2 weeks, interfere with work or relationships, or if you have thoughts of self-harm. Crisis helpline (India): iCall 9152987821, Vandrevala Foundation 1860-2662-345.

conditions.name: Hypertension Symptoms
conditions.description: High blood pressure often has no symptoms but can cause headaches, shortness of breath, or nosebleeds when severely elevated.
recommendations: Monitor blood pressure regularly
Reduce sodium intake and eat a heart-healthy diet
Exercise regularly — aim for 150 minutes per week
Manage stress and maintain a healthy weight
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If blood pressure readings consistently exceed 140/90 mmHg, or immediately if experiencing severe headache, chest pain, or vision problems.

conditions.name: Sunburn / Minor Burn
conditions.description: Damage to the skin caused by overexposure to ultraviolet radiation or contact with hot surfaces.
recommendations: Cool the burn with cool (not cold) running water for 10-20 minutes
Apply aloe vera gel or moisturizing lotion
Take ibuprofen for pain and inflammation
Stay hydrated and avoid further sun exposure
conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If burn covers a large area, causes large blisters, involves the face/joints/hands, or shows signs of infection.

fallback.name: General Health Inquiry
fallback.description: Your symptoms require more specific details for an accurate assessment.
recommendations: Please describe your symptoms in more detail
Note when symptoms started and any triggers
Consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis
If symptoms are severe or worsening, seek medical attention promptly
fallback.when_to_see_doctor: If you are unsure about your symptoms or they are causing significant concern, always consult a healthcare professional.
